code.text: Awake left frontal craniotomy with cortical and subcortical language and motor mapping and fluorescence-guided resection: gross total resection of the enhancing tumor, stopped at the mapped language sites. Pathology: glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4 (necrosis and microvascular proliferation; IDH1 R132H immunostain negative and no IDH1 or IDH2 mutation on sequencing; ATRX retained; TERT promoter mutation; EGFR amplification; gain of chromosome 7 and loss of chromosome 10; CDKN2A homozygous deletion; histone H3 and BRAF wild-type). MGMT promoter methylated by pyrosequencing. Inpatient stay of three days, with mechanical and then low-molecular-weight heparin prophylaxis against venous thromboembolism from the day after surgery

MRI of the brain with and without contrast within 48 hours of surgery: no residual enhancing tumor; expected postoperative blood products; small area of restricted diffusion at the posterior margin from surgery; edema and midline shift less

Outpatient physical therapy assessment: mild weakness of the right hand and hip flexors after surgery; the left calf, weakened by polio in childhood, slightly smaller than the right with full strength; Timed Up and Go 9 seconds; home exercise program, home safety review and a fall plan
External beam radiotherapy to the resection cavity and margin, 60 Gy in 30 daily fractions over six weeks, with daily temozolomide; given in full on schedule

Outpatient palliative care consultation alongside cancer treatment: symptoms, coping, her understanding of the illness, goals and wishes, support for her family, and advance care planning; she named a health care agent (recorded in the confidential part of the chart) and completed an advance directive

MRI of the brain with and without contrast four weeks after chemoradiation: thin, smooth enhancement along the resection cavity with no nodular or new enhancement; FLAIR change around the cavity slightly less than after surgery; no new lesion. Treatment-related change; no progression (RANO 2.0); this scan is the new baseline
Advance care planning conversation, about 20 minutes, reviewing the advance directive completed with palliative care

text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Urgent neuro-oncology consultation within one week, together with neurosurgery, to review the brain MRI with her and plan diagnosis and treatment if it shows a tumor
  • New progressive focal neurologic symptoms are imaged promptly: MRI of the brain with and without contrast within 24 hours, with same-day emergency care if she worsens, has a seizure, vomits or becomes drowsy; blood count, chemistry and A1c; no driving until the cause is known
  • Dexamethasone only for edema causing symptoms, at the lowest effective dose (4 mg twice a day), with famotidine and glucose checks, and tapered off as soon as possible after surgery
  • CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis to exclude another primary; functional MRI with tractography; awake craniotomy with language and motor mapping for maximal safe resection; MRI within 48 hours; integrated WHO CNS5 diagnosis with IDH1 R132H immunostaining and IDH1 and IDH2 sequencing, ATRX, TERT promoter, EGFR, chromosome 7 and 10, CDKN2A, histone H3, BRAF and MGMT promoter methylation
  • No antiseizure prophylaxis, because she has had no seizure; seizure first aid taught to her and her household; levetiracetam if a seizure occurs
  • Venous thromboembolism: mechanical and then low-molecular-weight heparin prophylaxis in hospital after surgery; no routine prophylaxis at home; she is taught the signs of leg clot and pulmonary embolism and to report them the same day
  • Radiotherapy 60 Gy in 30 fractions with temozolomide 75 mg/m2 daily, then six cycles of temozolomide 150 to 200 mg/m2 on days 1 to 5 of each 28-day cycle; Pneumocystis prophylaxis during concurrent treatment and while lymphopenia lasts; antiemetic before each dose; blood count weekly during chemoradiation and on day 22 of each adjuvant cycle; liver tests at baseline, mid-cycle 1 and before each cycle; MRI four weeks after radiotherapy and then every two to three months, read by RANO 2.0; clinical trial screening
  • Tumor-treating fields with adjuvant temozolomide, worn at least 18 hours a day, with scalp checks and skin care
  • Falls and mobility from the first visit: home safety review, fall plan, physical therapy assessment once the treatment plan is set, and a check at every visit of strength in both legs, since new right-sided weakness adds to a left leg weakened by polio in childhood; watch for new weakness, fatigue or pain that could signal post-polio syndrome
  • Early palliative care alongside cancer treatment: symptoms, coping, goals and advance care planning, and support for the people she chooses
  • Distress and depression screening at each visit, plain explanations with written information, and help to keep working as long as she wishes; she decides who receives information

resource.title: Wilma Rudolph synthetic care plan
resource.description: Recognize new progressive neurologic symptoms (morning headache, word-finding pauses and a clumsy hand) as a reason for prompt contrast MRI of the brain in a 54-year-old Black woman who survived childhood polio, and then manage a newly diagnosed glioblastoma to current standards: dexamethasone only for symptomatic edema, at the lowest dose and tapered early, with glucose and stomach protection; no seizure prophylaxis when no seizure has occurred; CT to exclude another primary; awake craniotomy with language and motor mapping for maximal safe resection and an MRI within 48 hours; the WHO CNS5 2021 integrated diagnosis with IDH, TERT, EGFR, chromosome 7 and 10 and MGMT promoter methylation; radiotherapy 60 Gy in 30 fractions with daily temozolomide and Pneumocystis prophylaxis, then adjuvant temozolomide with tumor-treating fields; blood count and liver test monitoring; RANO 2.0 response assessment that allows for pseudoprogression; venous thromboembolism awareness; fall prevention for a woman whose new right-sided weakness meets a left leg weakened by polio in childhood; and early palliative care with advance care planning alongside treatment, on the NCCN CNS cancers guideline, the EANO 2021 diffuse glioma guideline and the ASCO-SNO glioma guideline. Her childhood care, given at a Black medical school because care nearer home was not offered to her, frames the commitment to equal access to a brain tumor center and clinical trials.
